prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — do you want specific contractor names in Joplin, or guidance on how to find and vet a reliable contractor? 

If you want names, tell me:
- what type of work (kitchen, bathroom, whole‑house remodel, roof, siding, foundation, electrical, plumbing, etc.)
- approximate scope and budget
- desired start date
With that I can suggest a short list of types of contractors to contact and sample questions to ask.

If you want guidance now, here are reliable steps and resources to find a good contractor in Joplin, MO:

Where to look
- Google Maps & Google Reviews (search terms like “home remodel contractor Joplin MO”)
- Better Business Bureau (BBB.org) for ratings and complaint history
- Angi (Angie’s List), HomeAdvisor, Houzz and Yelp for customer reviews and portfolios
- Nextdoor and local Facebook community groups for neighbor recommendations
- Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce for established local businesses
- Ask local real estate agents or recent home‑remodel neighbors for referrals
- Joplin City Building Division for information about required permits and any local contractor lists

How to vet contractors
- Verify they carry liability insurance and worker’s compensation (ask for certificates)
- Check licenses: Missouri does not have a single statewide general‑contractor license — confirm any trade licensing (electrical, plumbing, HVAC) and check local Joplin requirements and permits
- Ask for local references (ask to see recent projects in Joplin) and actually call or visit if possible
- Review portfolios/photos of completed jobs similar to yours
- Look up their BBB profile and online reviews for patterns (how they resolve issues)
- Get at least three written, itemized bids to compare scope and materials
- Confirm estimated timeline, payment schedule (avoid large up‑front payments), and what happens for change orders
- Require a written contract listing scope, materials, start/end dates, payment schedule, warranty on labor and materials, and lien release language

Questions to ask a contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?
- Do you have local references from the past year?
- Who will be on site and who is the point of contact?
- What is included in this bid (materials, demo, finishes)? What is excluded?
- How do you handle change orders, delays, and unforeseen conditions?
- What is the recommended payment schedule and do you provide a written contract?
- Do you obtain permits and arrange inspections?

Red flags
- Unwillingness to provide proof of insurance or references
- Extremely low bids that are much lower than others
- Demands for large cash up‑front payments
- No written contract or vague scope
- Poor or nonexistent local references and many unresolved complaints online

If you want, tell me your project details and I’ll draft:
- a short list of likely contractor types to contact
- three sample contractors (if you want me to look up names I’ll need permission to search online now, or you can copy/paste local listings you’re considering)
- a script to call or message them and a sample contract checklist you can use

Which would you prefer?
